automation_evidence.quote: AnomaMind operates through a coarse-to-fine workflow that first localizes suspicious intervals, then constructs diagnostic evidence through tool interaction, and finally refines anomaly decisions through self-reflection.

metric_evidence.quote: Extensive experiments under both in-domain and cross-domain settings demonstrate consistent performance gains, validating the effectiveness of tool-augmented reasoning for TSAD.

evidence.quote: Detection Tool Ablation: As shown in Table V, the full AnomaMind achieves the best overall performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed detection tools.

practical_problems.note: tool ablation removes knowledge memory (domain knowledge and mined anomaly patterns) among other tools; effect reported as F1 drop calibration: whole-tool ablation (knowledge memory among several tools), not an exogenous context source removed.

evidence.quote: cross-domain settings. The in-domain setting trains a separate model for each dataset, while the cross-domain setting trains a unified model on all training splits

practical_problems.note: domain shift is motivating; the cross-domain setting trains on all datasets and tests on their splits, so no held-out shift is evaluated

evidence.quote: Figure 5 illustrates a representative coarse-to-fine detection case.

practical_problems.note: evidence construction shown in one case study; no faithfulness or reviewer evaluation

summary: Turns anomaly detection into a tool-using, self-verifying workflow with an RL-trained detector; reports higher F1 than baselines on four datasets in-domain and unified-training settings, with ablations, but no held-out shift or evidence-faithfulness test.
